description: First review batch for The Sound Maze. Each target is spoken aloud; the learner selects its spelling. Draft content is not yet wired into the live game.

questions.explain: The vowel in cat is /æ/, as in apple. Cut has /ʌ/, cot has /ɒ/ in many accents, and cap ends with /p/ rather than /t/.
Pen has the short /e/ sound. Pan has /æ/, pin has /ɪ/, and pun has /ʌ/.
Sit has the short /ɪ/ sound. Sat has /æ/, set has /e/, and suit has a different vowel sound.
Fan begins with /f/, made without vocal-cord vibration. Van begins with /v/, while man and pan begin with /m/ and /p/.
Ten begins with /t/, a short voiceless sound. Den begins with /d/, then begins with /ð/, and Ken begins with /k/.
Rice begins with /r/. Rise has the same beginning but a different final sound (/z/), while lice and nice begin with /l/ and /n/.
Bag ends with /g/. Back ends with /k/, bat with /t/, and bad with /d/.
Cap ends with the unvoiced /p/ sound. Cab ends with /b/, cat with /t/, and can with /n/.
Rice ends with /s/. Right ends with /t/, ride with /d/, and rise with /z/.
Cake has a final silent e, which makes the a say its name /eɪ/. The other words have short vowel sounds.
Bike has the long /aɪ/ sound written with i and a final silent e. The other choices have short vowel sounds.
Home has the long /əʊ/ sound written with o and a final silent e. Ham, hum, and hop have short vowel sounds.
